The Ijtihaad of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) and Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA)

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Yazeed reports that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) was questioned about anything and the reply was to be found in the Qur'aan, he would state what was in the Qur'aan. If it was not found in the Qur'aan but Rasulullaah ﷺ had spoken about it, he would say what Rasulullaah ﷺ said. If it was not found in the Qur'aan and Rasulullaah ﷺ had not spoken about it, but Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) or Hadhrat Umar (RA) had mentioned it, he would say what Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) or Hadhrat Umar (RA) said. However, if it was not found in the Qur'aan and if Rasulullaah ﷺ, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA) had not spoken about it, he would practise Ijtihaad." [^2]
Another narration states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "When we receive corroboration (to an injunction), we would not equate anything else to it (and would readily practise it)." [^3]

Hadhrat Masrooq narrates that when he once questioned Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) about something, Hadhrat Ubay (RA) asked, "Has it already happened?" When he was informed that it had not happened, he said, "Then grant us respite until it happens and then when it does, we will be able to practise Ijtihaad." [^4]

The Statement of Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla concerning the Cautiousness of the Sahabah (RA)

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla
blocks.text: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla says, "I met a hundred and twenty Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ in the Masjid. When any of them narrated a Hadith, he wished that his brother (another Sahabi (RA)) had done it for him and whenever he issued a Fatwaa, he also wished that his brother had done it for him." [^5]
Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol.2 Pg.57).
